title: Sprig and Dandelion's Big Puddle
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a meadow so soft and mellow, lived Sprig the squirrel and Dandelion the duck. Sprig loved to amble and collect little treasures. Dandelion loved to paddle and swish in the water.

Every day was quiet and peaceful. Sprig ambled up his old oak tree with a walnut in his paws. Dandelion swished to the shimmering pond and made small rings on the water with her feet.

Until one day, a very large puddle shone in the meadow. Sprig found a smooth walnut shell, just like a little boat. Dandelion saw the big inviting puddle and waddled closer, her feathers bright as morning.

Because of that, Sprig nudged the walnut shell to the edge of the puddle. Dandelion ambled over. Sprig hopped inside their new boat, and Dandelion settled in beside him. “Shall we go for a little paddle?” Dandelion whispered. “Oh, yes please!” chirped Sprig.

Because of that, they gently pushed away. Dandelion’s webbed feet moved surely, and the water swirled softly. A gentle breeze made their boat twirl around and around. Sprig giggled. Dandelion quacked with quiet joy. They twirled and twirled, feeling wonderfully warm and peaceful, while the walnut shell went shush-shush on the shining puddle.

Until finally, the sun began to lower its golden head. The breeze softened to a whisper, like a lullaby. Sprig felt a tickle in his nose, and a wide stretch pulled at his whiskers. “Oh, I’m feeling quite sleepy,” he said. Dandelion’s bright eyes grew heavy. They paddled back to the grassy edge and ambled to their cozy homes. Sprig snuggled deep into his soft nest. Dandelion tucked herself into her downy bed.

Ever since then, Sprig and Dandelion often share gentle paddles in their walnut boat. When the boat twirls, they smile. When the stars begin to twinkle, they go home. Moonbeams light the meadow, and two sleepy friends drift off, safe and sound.
